propositions: Build and validate a one-time history-strip operational script using stock Git plumbing (fast-export/fast-import) that removes .bridge_state/ and .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ prefixes from all historical revisions while preserving commit and merge topology.

Prove the rewrite on a scratch unfiltered --no-tags clone before any remote publication, asserting commit/merge counts, tree identity after dynamic re-add, absence of target history except HEAD, and final pack size under 150 MB.
Reject partial-clone repositories with a clear error message and require a fresh unfiltered clone; refuse to push or modify remote refs during dry-run execution.
Parse fast-export data blocks by byte length rather than line-based filtering to safely preserve commit messages that begin with `M ` or `D ` command bytes.
Dynamically derive the re-add file set from git ls-tree instead of hardcoded lists to accommodate future .bridge_state/ extensions and prove four-file survival.
Verify source remote branch and protected tag remain unchanged after dry-run, and confirm the protected tag is absent from the rewritten scratch clone before pack measurement.
